title: Chapter 15
content:
Jakyeong stared with hollow, glazed eyes at the wisps of smoke vanishing into the bathroom exhaust vent. He’d spent the entire night tossing and turning until daybreak, his mind completely shot. He’d hoped a freezing shower might shake off the mental fog, but it hadn't done a damn thing.

Frayed by raw, relentless stress, his body practically screamed for nicotine. He pulled on his e-cigarette, dragging on it in rapid succession until his lungs burned. Only then did the tightness in his chest ease, allowing a fragile semblance of calm to settle over his nerves.

Sprawling his long limbs across the dry porcelain tub, the visceral memory of last night crashed back over him.

Even through the drug-induced delirium, the phantom sensation of that foreign intrusion between his thighs remained sickeningly vivid. Fucking dog. He’d landed a solid heel to the bastard's jaw, but if he had followed his true instincts, he would have slit Kang Il-hyun’s throat on the spot. Worse still, even after he’d retreated to his bedroom, the lingering aphrodisiac had kept his body agonizingly wound up—forcing him to drag himself into the bathroom to jerk off just to get an ounce of sleep.

The sheer indignity of it made his skin crawl.

"Fucking piece of shit," he hissed, glaring murderously at the ceiling.

As he ground his molars together, his encrypted phone vibrated against the porcelain. It was Wang Han. The second he swiped to answer, his partner’s warm, familiar voice came through the line. But Wang Han caught the dark, gravelly dip in Jakyeong’s tone immediately and pressed to know what was wrong.

"Nothing. I'm fine."

[Then why do you sound so drained? You're not sick, are you?]

Jakyeong shifted his head, looking down between his legs. His lower back and tailbone still carried a dull, phantom ache, but he would rather eat a bullet than confess that humiliation out loud.

"What's got you calling so early?"

[Where are you right now? Your tracker showed active pinging last night.]

"I used it on an external target. Send the full breadcrumb route—from the first ping to the final stop—directly to my phone."

Last night, Jakyeong had covertly slapped a micro-GPS tracker beneath the passenger seat of the sports car driven by the man with the dokkaebi goblin tattoo. He couldn't fully explain why he’d done it. Was it lingering empathy for the little drop-runner who mirrored his own childhood? Or an obsession to uncover the syndicate that had butchered his parents? Either way, checking the coordinates in person would provide the answers.

"Hey, Hyung. That dossier you gave me on Kang Il-hyun... was that everything?"

[What do you mean?]

The question of whether Kang Il-hyun was into men died on the tip of Jakyeong’s tongue. He muttered a vague brush-off and hung up. Tossing the phone into the tub, he stared blankly upward for a moment before hauling himself to his feet.

Stepping onto the edge of the bathtub, he reached up and pressed his palms against the exhaust vent. Poking his fingers through the narrow intake slats, he yanked down with all his might, but the metal wouldn't budge. He shifted his grip and pushed upward from the opposite side—and felt a faint give.

Oh?

Bracing his footing, he gave a hard, controlled shove. The vent cover popped free from its housing, unlatching cleanly from the ceiling. He flicked on his phone’s flashlight, illuminating the ductwork beyond a thick blanket of gray dust. He couldn't tell where the shaft led, but the clearance was far tighter than he’d hoped. Squeezing his shoulders through would be a miserable, tight crawl at best.

Damn it.

Disappointed, he snapped the panel back into place and dropped onto the edge of the tub.

["You should have said so earlier. It's not like I have anything to hide from you."]

Il-hyun’s effortless compliance in showing him the basement was still nagging at him. If he simply asked where the master safe was, would the man just point it out? Based on last night's disaster, Il-hyun clearly harbored some twisted curiosity toward him—whether he just enjoyed tormenting a timid rich kid or genuinely intended to take him to bed.

What if I just play along, let him take my ass once, and sweet-talk the safe's location out of him? Who knows? Maybe he’d even hand over the key.

The terrifying mental image of himself panting beneath Kang Il-hyun made his face instantly warp in sheer disgust. Fuck no. I’ve lost my goddamn mind. Greed has its limits, but that's pure insanity.

He slapped himself across both cheeks to knock some sense into his head, then climbed out of the bathtub and walked out into the bedroom.

Collapsing onto the king-sized mattress, exhaustion dragged his eyelids shut. He drifted off without realizing it, only waking up when the afternoon sun was already burning through the curtains. Hunger gnawed at his stomach, prompting him to head downstairs for a meal.

Cooking duties in the estate fell to the senior housekeeper, and her culinary prowess was nothing short of miraculous. Whether it was international cuisine or traditional Korean home cooking, everything she prepared was perfectly tuned to Jakyeong’s palate.

He had descended about two-thirds of the central staircase when the low hum of conversation from the living room made his boots freeze on the steps.

Sitting on the lounge sofa, casually conversing with Park Tae-soo, was Kang Il-hyun.

Why the hell is this guy still lounging around the house at this hour?

Jakyeong whipped around on his heel, making a frantic, silent dash back toward the second-floor landing—only for Il-hyun's smooth baritone to lasso him from behind.

"Yi-an. Where are you off to?"

Jakyeong halted mid-stride, grinding his teeth in frustration. Fucking bastard.

Forcing his expression to smooth out, he turned around with a polite, picture-perfect smile. "Good morning, Executive Director Kang."

"It's past lunchtime."

"Ah... right. I overslept a bit..."

"You must have been exhausted. Did you have trouble sleeping last night?"

Jakyeong’s fists clenched instinctively behind his back. The sheer, shameless audacity of this man was breathtaking. Was he deliberately trying to push his buttons, or had early-onset dementia already rotted the bastard's brain? If your goal was to piss me off, congratulations, you piece of shit.

"I suffer from a bit of insomnia..." Jakyeong murmured, keeping his voice meek.

"Oh, dear. My home must not be comfortable enough for you."

"Not at all. You’ve been so exceptionally hospitable, I’m resting very comfortably."

As they exchanged the hollow pleasantries, Il-hyun slowly raised his hand, crooking his index finger in a lazy, rhythmic beckon—the universal gesture for calling over a stray dog.

Jakyeong’s smile tightened as he completely ignored the summon. Offering a crisp bow, he remarked that Il-hyun must be busy with work, turned, and marched back toward the guest wing on the second floor.

He prayed the man wouldn't follow, but naturally, heavy footsteps closed in behind him.

Reaching his suite's threshold, Jakyeong turned to find Il-hyun standing bare inches from his chest.

"Did you... have something else to say...?"

"The security camera will be removed tomorrow," Il-hyun said smoothly. "If you have any valuables in the bedroom, lock them in the safe beforehand."

The word safe made Jakyeong’s internal alarms flare with interest.

"The... safe?"

"Haven't you seen it? The bed frame is customized with an integrated vault. I’ve had the system factory-reset, so you can program your own passcode."

The unexpected revelation sparked a flicker of calculated excitement in Jakyeong's chest. "Fascinating... Are all the rooms in the house fitted with safes like that?"

Il-hyun nodded. "Generally."

I see. So your master bedroom has one too?

Jakyeong probed with his eyes, but Il-hyun offered no further details. The sheer ease with which the information was given immediately raised Jakyeong's guard. He had let his defenses down last night and walked straight into a trap.

He stared intently into Il-hyun's dark pupils, trying to read the game beneath the surface. Il-hyun looked down at him, letting out a low, amused chuckle.

"And regarding last night... let's pretend it never happened. It would only make things awkward between us."

Jakyeong forced a wide, utterly oblivious smile. "Last night...? Did something happen?"

The moment the words left his mouth, Il-hyun reached a hand out toward his shoulder. Startled, Jakyeong instinctively took a sharp step back.

The corner of Il-hyun's lips curled into a wicked, knowing crescent.

"See? You remember perfectly."

Jakyeong held the smile on his face, but inside, his blood was boiling. He mentally cursed himself for flinching like a rookie.

Telling Jakyeong he’d see him after work, Il-hyun turned and retraced his steps down the hall. Watching the man's broad back disappear down the corridor, Jakyeong bared his teeth in a silent snarl.

Yeah, laugh while you still have a head on your shoulders.

"Sorry about last night, man. You didn't say anything weird to my brother, did you?"

Kang Seok-joo arrived to see Jakyeong shortly after lunch. The arrogant kingpin who had swaggered through the underground club last night had shrunk back into a pathetic, cowering puppy the moment he stepped foot inside Il-hyun’s residence.

"I didn't say anything."

"I knew I could count on you!"

Seok-joo threw an arm around Jakyeong’s shoulders with the familiarity of a lifelong friend. He went on to gush about how the girl from last night had fallen head-over-heels for Jakyeong, even volunteering the information that she was the only daughter of an elite, high-ranking legal dynasty.

"She’s totally hooked on you. She’s been blowing up my phone all morning begging for your number. Come on, she’s gorgeous and her body is insane—don't you want to hook up with her?"

Jakyeong gave an awkward, sheepish smile, pushing his horn-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose. "I don't know..."

"Wait, don't tell me... you're still a virgin?"

"A what?"

Seok-joo curled his fingers into an explicit, rhythmic hand gesture simulating intercourse.

Jakyeong swallowed a chuckle. He’d lost his virginity at fifteen to an older Chinese girl living next door in the slums. Since then, he’d slept with more women than he could count, though contracts and assignments had kept his private life bone-dry in recent years.

Taking Jakyeong's stunned silence for wide-eyed innocence, Seok-joo’s eyes lit up with predatory excitement.

"Perfect! There's a... unique kind of exhibition tomorrow. We're going."

Jakyeong had no idea what the kid was planning, but it clearly had nothing to do with fine art. Judging by the depraved grin on Seok-joo’s face, it was bound to be degenerate.

"Is your friend coming too?"

"Friend? Which one?"

"The one who drove me home last night. Things were so chaotic I didn't even get to properly thank him..."

"Ah, forget about him. He only gave you a ride because I told him to."

"Are you two close?"

Seok-joo narrowed his eyes, chewing on the question before delivering his verdict. "Less like friends, more like business partners. I've got some personal capital invested in his ventures."

Catching himself oversharing, Seok-joo quickly backtracked. "That’s strictly between us, by the way. Don't go running your mouth to my brother."

"I'm not really one to gossip about other people's business..."

Seok-joo grinned, clapping Jakyeong on the shoulder in approval. Without further prompting, he began casually spilling details about Choi Ki-tae. When Jakyeong steered the conversation toward the tattoo on Ki-tae's arm, Seok-joo explained that the ink wasn't a syndicate insignia—Ki-tae had simply copied the exact design from his own father out of filial admiration.

Jakyeong recalled the menacing figure from his childhood memories, the pieces locking into place.

The brute with the four-horned goblin... was likely Choi Ki-tae's father.
